topics.definition: Virtualization creates virtual versions of computing resources such as servers, storage and networks.
topics.example: Running multiple VMs on one server

topics.definition: A hypervisor manages virtual machines. Type 1 runs on hardware; Type 2 runs on a host operating system.
tips: Type 1 is commonly used in data centers.

topics.definition: A VM is an isolated software-based computer with its own operating system.
tips: Each VM has dedicated virtual resources.

topics.definition: Virtual storage pools physical storage into logical storage resources.
Virtual networking connects virtual machines using software-defined networks.
VMs virtualize hardware with separate operating systems, while containers share the host operating system.
tips: Containers are generally lighter than VMs.

topics.definition: Virtualization is used in cloud computing, testing, disaster recovery and server consolidation.
Monitor resource usage, secure virtual machines and keep hypervisors updated.
